title: A discount bigger than the invoice is shared by size and both rows end at $0.00
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have two active staff members at the test location with their "Sales Representative" switch on: sales rep A and sales rep B.
  • Use a customer with no Sales Representative assigned, set as tax exempt so that no tax applies to its invoices.
  • Make sure the test location's Shop Supplies Charge is 0% and nothing else is invoiced at the test location today.
  • Create an open, uninvoiced work order for this test for that customer with one labor line of 1.00 hour at $100.00 ($100.00), one part sold at $50.00 and a non-taxable whole-invoice discount of $200.00 (not on any line), with Labor set to sales rep A and Parts set to sales rep B.
  • Open the work order in a desktop browser at least 1024 pixels wide.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Invoice the work order.
  2. Open Reports > Sales By Representative.
  3. Set the date range to today.
  4. Expand sales rep A.
  5. Expand sales rep B.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The invoice total is $0.00.
  • The discount does not take it below zero (100.00 + 50.00 − 200.00 would be −50.00, so $50.00 is added back).

Step 2:

  • The Sales By Representative report opens.

Step 3:

  • The report shows today's date range.

Step 4:

  • The work order's invoice has one row under sales rep A, its Labor row.
  • That row shows Labor Invoiced $100.00.
  • Its Adjustments reads ($100.00), its share of the −$150.00 net whole-invoice amount (100 ÷ 150 × 150).
  • Its subtotal is $0.00.

Step 5:

  • Its Parts row under sales rep B shows Parts Invoiced $50.00.
  • Its Adjustments reads ($50.00) (50 ÷ 150 × 150).
  • Its subtotal is $0.00.
  • $0.00 + $0.00 = $0.00, the invoice total.
  • Neither row goes below zero.
  • The report total for the invoice is $0.00.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11269 (Story 5, Credit each side on the invoice and in Sales By Representative)

  • S5-R6: “Whole-invoice fees and discounts are shared between the Labor and the Parts rows in proportion to each side's labor or parts dollars after that side's line fees and discounts, measured by size whatever their sign. The adjustment that stops a non-taxable discount from taking the subtotal below zero is a whole-invoice amount and is shared the same way. Example: labor $600.00, parts $400.00, shop supplies $30.00, whole-invoice discount ($50.00). The Labor row gets $30.00 supplies and ($30.00); the Parts row gets ($20.00). Subtotals $600.00 and $380.00 add up to $980.00. Each row shows its share in its Adjustments column.”

From: Chris Ward's answers to the Splitting Sales Representatives question sheet (answers 1 to 38, 19 Oct 2026; answers 39 and 40, 21 Oct 2026), read 22 Oct 2026

  • Chris Ward's answer 22: “22. (a) as the feature spec. Yes, the Sales By Representative definition changes to the row's share.”

From: Tech plan "Splitting Sales Representatives — Technical Implementation Plan" (dated 14 Oct 2026, planned against PRD version 8; uploaded 19 Oct 2026 and again, byte-identical, 22 Oct 2026), read in full 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan, line fees and the whole-invoice pool (section 8.2): “`invoice_level_adjustments` holds only the whole-invoice pool (`Invoice.orm.xml:58-68`: "scopes whole_wo / whole_parts_sale, the processing fee, the legacy invoice.discount rate and the §5 subtotal floor")”
  • Tech plan, end-to-end test N1 (section 7): “a whole-work-order $50 flat taxable discount (avoids the non-taxable clamp)”
